pack_name: The Hunt Expedition — Content Pack v1

venue_context.checkpoint_note: Organizer must choose and physically place cards/QR codes at safe, permitted locations; no specific campus placement is assumed.

game_rules.level_unlock_rule: Levels 2–5 unlock only after all required questions in the previous level are solved.
game_rules.level_5_order_rule: Questions 41–45 must be solved in strict sequence; each requires the immediately previous question.
game_rules.winner_rule: Solving all 45 questions qualifies a team for physical treasure verification but does not itself determine the winner. The first eligible team verified by an authenticated marshal wins.

questions.title: The Silent Keeper
questions.participant_prompt: I have pages but am not a tree. I hold stories but never speak. What am I?

hints.text: Think of something you read.
It has bound pages.
Consider the common bound reading volume with printed pages found on library shelves.

questions.title: The More You Take
questions.participant_prompt: The more steps you take, the more of these you leave behind. What are they?

hints.text: You leave them while moving.
They may appear in dust or sand.
Consider the visible trail or indentations left behind by each stride of your footwear.

questions.title: Clock Angle
questions.participant_prompt: At 3:15, what is the smaller angle between the hands of an analogue clock in degrees? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: The minute hand is at 90°.
The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute. At 15 minutes past the hour, calculate how far it has moved beyond its starting position.
Multiply 15 minutes by 0.5 degrees per minute to determine how far the hour hand moved beyond 90 degrees.

questions.title: Odd One Out
questions.participant_prompt: Which does not belong: triangle, square, circle, cube?

hints.text: Three are flat shapes.
One is a 3D solid.
Name the three-dimensional Platonic solid whose six bounding faces are all identical squares.

questions.title: Letter Steps
questions.participant_prompt: Continue: A, C, F, J, O, __.

hints.text: Look at the gaps.
The jumps are +2,+3,+4,+5.
Advance 6 positions forward in the alphabet from letter O.

questions.title: Library Code
questions.participant_prompt: Using A=1 through Z=26, decode 3-1-20.

hints.text: Convert numbers to letters.
Shift the final letter W back by three alphabet positions to complete the word.

questions.title: Two Fathers
questions.participant_prompt: Two fathers and two sons share three apples, one each. How many people?

hints.text: The relationships can overlap.
Think of three generations.
Map the family roles to distinct people: grandfather, father, son. How many unique individuals appear in that chain?

questions.title: Battery Hours
questions.participant_prompt: Four batteries each power a torch for 2 hours, one at a time. How many total hours does the torch run? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: Add each battery’s duration.
Four batteries, two hours each.
Calculate the total run time by evaluating 4 batteries multiplied by 2 hours each.

questions.title: Mirror Letter
questions.participant_prompt: Which capital letter is vertically symmetrical: A, F, G, or R?

hints.text: Left and right halves must match.
Only one option has vertical symmetry.
Test a vertical fold line down the center of each letter; choose the first letter of the alphabet.

questions.title: Expedition End
questions.participant_prompt: What letter ends both EXPEDITION and DESTINATION?

hints.text: Check the last letter of each word.
Both words finish with the same letter.
Inspect the final character shared by the suffix '-TION' in both words.

questions.title: Caesar Shift
questions.participant_prompt: Shift each letter one place backward: DBU. Decode it.

hints.text: Move each letter back one.
D→C, B→A.
Shift the third letter U back by one position to complete the three-letter animal name.

questions.title: Binary Trail
questions.participant_prompt: Convert binary 1010 to decimal.

hints.text: Use place values 8,4,2,1.
Sum the active binary place values 8 and 2.

questions.title: Pattern Lock
questions.participant_prompt: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, __.

hints.text: Find the differences.
Following the increment pattern of even numbers, add 12 to the previous term 30.

questions.title: Anagram Signal
questions.participant_prompt: Rearrange LISTEN to make a word meaning quiet.

hints.text: Use all six letters.
It is an anagram of LISTEN.
Rearrange all six letters starting with S-I to spell the opposite of noisy.

questions.title: Three Switches
questions.participant_prompt: Three switches outside a closed room control an incandescent bulb inside. You may enter the room only once. Besides light, what physical property of the bulb allows you to identify which switch was turned on? (Enter one word)

hints.text: Use the bulb's thermal state.
A bulb that was turned on stays warm for a while.
Name the thermal energy produced by electrical resistance in the filament that you can feel with your hand.

questions.title: HTTPS
questions.participant_prompt: What does HTTPS primarily provide for a web connection? (Enter as a two-word phrase)

hints.text: It protects data in transit.
It uses a security protocol.
Combine the adjective for cipher-scrambled data with the noun for a network link.

questions.title: Number Cipher
questions.participant_prompt: Using A=1, CODE is 3-15-4-5. What is the sum?

hints.text: Add 3, 15, 4, and 5.
Evaluate the sum: 18 plus 9.

questions.title: Logic Line
questions.participant_prompt: Mira is ahead of Sam. Sam is ahead of Jo. Who is last?

hints.text: Order them front to back.
Mira, then Sam, then the remaining person.
Identify the final two-letter name trailing behind Sam in the sequence.

questions.title: QR Knowledge
questions.participant_prompt: A QR code is what kind of code? (Enter as a three-word phrase)

hints.text: It uses a square pattern.
It encodes data in two dimensions.
Spell out the full three-word phrase describing a grid pattern that encodes data across horizontal and vertical axes.

questions.title: Reverse Trail
questions.participant_prompt: Reverse LEVEL. What word do you get?

hints.text: Read right to left.
It is a palindrome.
Spell the word backward letter by letter, noting that reading right-to-left preserves the original word.

questions.title: Truth and Lie
questions.participant_prompt: Exactly one statement is true. A: “B is lying.” B: “A and I are both lying.” Who tells the truth?

hints.text: B cannot be telling the truth.
If B were truthful, B’s claim contradicts itself.
Since statement B creates a self-contradiction and must be false, choose the person whose statement correctly identified B's dishonesty.

questions.title: Grid Coordinates
questions.participant_prompt: Start at (2,3). Move 4 east and 2 south. Final coordinates? (Format: (x,y) with parentheses)

hints.text: East increases x; south decreases y.
Evaluate the coordinates (2+4, 3-2) and write the resulting pair inside parentheses.

questions.title: Hexadecimal
questions.participant_prompt: Convert hexadecimal 2F to decimal.

hints.text: F equals 15.
Calculate: 32 plus 15.

questions.title: Three Boxes
questions.participant_prompt: Boxes labelled APPLES, ORANGES, MIXED all have wrong labels. From which box should you draw one fruit to identify all boxes?

hints.text: Every box carries an incorrect label. One label describes a mixture — that label is definitely wrong about what is inside its box.
Pick a single fruit from the one box whose contents you can deduce with certainty, based solely on the wrong-label rule.
Its fruit identifies it; use the wrong-label rule for the other two.

questions.title: Bubble Sort
questions.participant_prompt: After one left-to-right bubble-sort pass ascending, what is [8,3,5,1]? (Format: comma-separated numbers, e.g. 1,2,3,4)

hints.text: Compare adjacent pairs.
Swap 8 with 3, then 8 with 5.
Perform the final swap of 8 with 1 so the largest value moves to the end, then write the sequence separated by commas.

questions.title: Network Route
questions.participant_prompt: Links A→B, B→C, and C→D take 4 ms, 7 ms, and 3 ms respectively. What is the total latency in milliseconds? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: Add link delays.
Compute the combined latency by evaluating 11 plus 3.

questions.title: Coin Probability
questions.participant_prompt: A fair coin is flipped twice. Probability of two heads? (Format: fraction x/y or decimal 0.xx)

hints.text: List HH, HT, TH, TT.
Only one outcome has two heads.
Divide the 1 favorable outcome by the 4 equally likely total outcomes.

questions.title: Handshake Count
questions.participant_prompt: Three people each shake hands with every other person once. Total handshakes?

hints.text: Count pairs, not people’s perspectives.
Pairs: AB, AC, BC.
Each unique pair shakes once: count the distinct pairings (AB, AC, BC). How many pairs does that give you?

questions.title: Hash Clue
questions.participant_prompt: A cryptographic hash function processes input data of any size to produce a fixed-length output known as a what? (Enter one word)

hints.text: It is not ordinary two-way encryption.
The fixed-length output is commonly called a message ______.
Complete the common cryptographic phrase 'message ______' with its standard six-letter noun.

questions.title: Sequence Deduction
questions.participant_prompt: Find the next number: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, __.

hints.text: Each term sums the previous two.
Calculate the sum of the last two Fibonacci numbers: 5 plus 8.

questions.title: Checkpoint Cipher
questions.participant_prompt: At an organizer-placed checkpoint card, decode 20-18-5-1-19-21-18-5 using A=1.

hints.text: Convert each number to a letter.
Translate the numbers 1, 19, 21, 18, and 5 into alphabet positions to complete the eight-letter word.

questions.title: Canteen Calculation
questions.participant_prompt: Three water bottles cost ₹20 each and two snacks cost ₹15 each. What is the total cost in rupees? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: Calculate each group.
Add the beverage subtotal (60) to the snack subtotal (30).

questions.title: Stage Geometry
questions.participant_prompt: A rectangular stage is 8 m by 5 m. What is its perimeter in meters? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: Perimeter=2×(length+width).
Evaluate the perimeter formula: 2 multiplied by 13 meters.

questions.title: Library Index
questions.participant_prompt: Take the first letter of LIBRARY and the last letter of READ. What two-letter code results?

hints.text: Use the positions specified.
LIBRARY begins L; READ ends D.
Combine the initial letter of LIBRARY with the terminal letter of READ in that order.

questions.title: Route Planning
questions.participant_prompt: A safe marked route P→Q→R→S takes 3, 5, and 4 minutes per leg. What is the total time in minutes? (Enter the number only)

hints.text: Add each leg.
Compute the total leg time by adding 8 minutes to 4 minutes.

questions.title: Error Detection
questions.participant_prompt: Using A=1, decode 3-1-20.

hints.text: Convert each number.
3=C and 1=A.
Convert the third number (20) into its alphabet position, and append it to the letters obtained from 3 and 1.

questions.title: Binary Checksum
questions.participant_prompt: Add binary 101 and 011. Give the answer in binary.

hints.text: Convert to decimal if easier.
Express the decimal sum 8 as a power of two in four-bit binary notation.

questions.title: Observation Card
questions.participant_prompt: An organizer-placed card shows ▲ ● ▲ ▲ ●. If ▲=1 and ●=0, what five-bit code is shown?

hints.text: Replace each symbol.
Write the five binary digits corresponding to triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, circle without spaces.

questions.title: Missing Number
questions.participant_prompt: Three consecutive even numbers sum to 42. What is the middle number?

hints.text: Represent them as n−2, n, n+2.
Their sum is 3n=42.
Divide the total sum 42 by 3 to find the middle even number n.

questions.title: Expedition Checkpoint
questions.participant_prompt: Take the first letter of COMPASS, last letter of MAP, and first letter of TRAIL. Code?

hints.text: Take only the requested positions.
C, P, T.
Concatenate the three extracted letters together without spaces or punctuation.

questions.title: Final Chain 1 — The Key
questions.participant_prompt: I have keys but no locks, space but no room, and you can enter but not go inside. What am I?

hints.text: It is used to type.
It has a Space bar and an Enter key.
Identify the primary peripheral device with alphanumeric keys and a space bar in front of you.

questions.title: Final Chain 2 — The Input
questions.participant_prompt: Using your answer to Q41, on a standard QWERTY keyboard what letter is immediately to the right of K?

hints.text: Find K on the home row.
The home row ends ... J K L.
Locate the key positioned directly between 'K' and the semicolon on the standard home row.

questions.title: Final Chain 3 — The Count
questions.participant_prompt: Take the letter from Q42. What is its position in the English alphabet?

hints.text: Use A=1.
K occupies the 11th position. Count one step forward in the alphabet from K to find the position of the letter from Q42.
Count one position past the 11th alphabet letter (K) to determine the position of the letter from Q42.

questions.title: Final Chain 4 — The Code
questions.participant_prompt: Convert the number from Q43 using A=1, B=2, ... Z=26. Which letter is it?

hints.text: Look up the twelfth letter.
Count through the alphabet.
Identify the single alphabet letter situated directly after 'K' in alphabet order.

questions.title: Final Chain 5 — The Word
questions.participant_prompt: Write the letter from Q44, then the first letter of TREASURE, then the last letter of HUNT. What code do you get?

hints.text: Start with Q44’s answer.
TREASURE begins T; HUNT ends T.
Place the letter from Q44 first, followed by the initial of TREASURE and the terminal of HUNT.

treasure_verification.instruction: Generate a high-entropy token after the treasure location and marshal procedure are finalized. Store only a verifier/hash in protected storage; never include the token in participant data.

import_warning: Generic JSON interchange format. Map fields to the reviewed Supabase schema and validate RPC contracts before import. Do not seed remote staging until separately authorized.
